title: Evaluating Expressions
sub: Plug in, with parentheses, and watch negatives

steps.html:
Evaluating Expressions

3a + 6b when a = 4, b = 1
3(4) + 6(1)
12 + 6 = 18
Replace each letter with its number in parentheses. Then follow PEMDAS.
say: Today: evaluating, which just means plugging numbers in for letters.
Three a plus six b, when a is four and b is one. Replace each letter with its number, in parentheses.
Three times four is twelve, six times one is six. Total, eighteen.
Always put the number in parentheses, then follow the order of operations.

steps.html:
Why parentheses matter: negatives

3x2 when x = −2
3(−2)2 = 3 × 4 = 12 ✓
without parentheses: 3 × −2² = 3 × −4 = −12 ✗
say: Parentheses really matter with negative numbers.
Three x squared, when x is negative two. Write three times negative two in parentheses, squared. Negative two squared is positive four. Three times four is twelve.
Skip the parentheses and you might square only the two, and get negative twelve. Wrong!
Evaluate three x squared minus four y, when x is negative two and y is four.
steps.okSay: Yes! Twelve minus sixteen is negative four.
steps.noSay: Not quite. Three times negative two squared is three times four, twelve. Four times four is sixteen. Twelve minus sixteen is negative four.

say: Evaluate x plus y, all squared, when x is one and y is five.
steps.okSay: Yes! One plus five is six, and six squared is thirty-six.
steps.noSay: Not quite. Do the parentheses first: one plus five is six. Six squared is thirty-six. Squaring each one separately gives twenty-six, which is wrong.

say: Great! Now 4 practice questions. You'll see the answer and an explanation after each one.
Last part: three checkpoint questions. Get two out of three to finish the lesson. You've got this!

steps.html:
Remember

1. Swap each letter for its number in parentheses.

2. Then PEMDAS.

3. (−2)2 = +4. (x + y)2: add first, then square.
say: Let's review. Swap each letter for its number, in parentheses.
Then follow the order of operations.
A negative squared is positive, and with a sum in parentheses, add first, then square. Nice work!
